claims.text: The target as-cast Mg-containing lightweight HEA has a density below 6 g/cm3.
The initial as-cast alloy is in a non-equilibrium, metastable state.
The initial alloy consists primarily of a single-phase solid solution with minimal intermetallic content.
Controlled sub-equilibrium annealing promotes Mg segregation and intermetallic nucleation without producing full equilibrium.
Differential diffusion rates and local thermodynamic driving forces cause Mg to leave the solid-solution matrix and segregate locally.
Mg preferentially enriches at grain boundaries during the proposed transformation.
Local Mg enrichment and matrix depletion trigger nucleation and growth of stable Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
The Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates form particularly at grain boundaries.
Annealed samples will have a greater volume fraction of discrete Mg-rich intermetallic compounds than the as-cast baseline.
Formation of Mg-rich intermetallics changes the local chemical and electrochemical environment.
The annealing-induced intermetallic structure promotes formation of a continuous, adherent, and protective oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
Annealed samples will exhibit improved high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast baseline.
Chemical and phase heterogeneity between Mg-rich intermetallics and the solid-solution matrix creates micro-galvanic cells in corrosive environments.
Micro-galvanic coupling changes the corrosion behavior of annealed samples relative to the homogeneous as-cast state.
The proposed oxidation behavior applies approximately over 500–900°C in air.
The proposed mechanism is limited to Mg-significant lightweight HEAs produced by rapid induction melting and subjected to partial-transforming annealing.
